name: Navigation Clarity
description: The interface makes it easy for users to understand where they are, where they can go next, and how to move through the website or web application without confusion.
aliases: navigation| wayfinding| menu clarity| information scent
examples: I could immediately find the settings page from the main menu.  The breadcrumb helped me understand where I was.  I felt lost after clicking into the dashboard.

name: Information Architecture
description: Content, pages, features, and controls are organized in a way that matches user expectations and supports efficient discovery.
aliases: content structure| page organization| site structure| hierarchy
examples: The categories made sense to me.  I expected billing to be under account settings.  Related options were scattered across different pages.

name: Label Clarity
description: Buttons, links, headings, form fields, and menu items use clear wording that helps users understand what each element does.
aliases: wording| microcopy| labels| terminology
examples: The button label told me exactly what would happen.  I did not understand what ‘Manage assets’ meant.  The field names were too technical.

name: Learnability
description: New users can understand how to use the interface without extensive instruction, training, or trial and error.
aliases: easy to learn| first-time use| onboarding| intuitiveness
examples: I understood how to start without reading help text.  It took me a few tries to figure out the workflow.  The onboarding made the feature easy to use.

name: Onboarding Guidance
description: The product provides useful first-time guidance, explanations, examples, or progressive hints that help users understand key actions.
aliases: tutorials| walkthroughs| getting started| guided setup
examples: The setup wizard helped me complete the first task.  The tooltip explained the new feature clearly.  I skipped onboarding and then did not know what to do.

name: Visual Hierarchy
description: The page uses layout, spacing, typography, contrast, and emphasis to make important information and actions stand out.
aliases: layout clarity| emphasis| scannability| priority
examples: The primary action was easy to spot.  Everything looked equally important.  I noticed the warning before submitting.

name: Content Readability
description: Text content is easy to read, scan, and understand, with appropriate length, structure, tone, and formatting.
aliases: readability| text clarity| plain language| scannable content
examples: The instructions were short and easy to follow.  The page had too much dense text.  The help article answered my question quickly.

name: Task Efficiency
description: Users can complete common tasks quickly with minimal unnecessary steps, repetition, waiting, or context switching.
aliases: efficiency| speed| workflow friction| productivity
examples: I completed the booking in just a few clicks.  I had to enter the same information twice.  The shortcut saved me time.

name: Workflow Continuity
description: The interface supports users through multi-step processes without losing context, progress, or user input.
aliases: flow continuity| process flow| task flow| progress preservation
examples: The progress indicator helped me know how many steps were left.  My form data disappeared when I went back.  I could pause and continue later.

name: Search and Filtering
description: Users can find specific content, records, products, or settings using effective search, filters, sorting, and result refinement.
aliases: findability| search| filters| sorting
examples: The filters helped me narrow the results quickly.  Search did not return the item I was looking for.  Sorting by date made the list easier to use.

name: Feedback and System Status
description: The interface clearly communicates what is happening, what has changed, and whether an action was successful, pending, or failed.
aliases: system feedback| status visibility| progress feedback| confirmation
examples: I saw a confirmation after saving.  The loading spinner showed the page was still working.  I clicked submit but nothing seemed to happen.

name: Error Prevention
description: The design helps users avoid mistakes before they happen through constraints, validation, confirmation, defaults, and clear guidance.
aliases: mistake prevention| safeguards| validation| constraints
examples: The form warned me before I entered an invalid date.  The delete confirmation prevented a serious mistake.  I accidentally submitted before finishing.

name: Error Recovery
description: When something goes wrong, the interface helps users understand the problem and recover without losing progress or becoming stuck.
aliases: error handling| recovery| correction| failure support
examples: The error message told me exactly how to fix the issue.  I could retry the upload after it failed.  The error page gave me no way back.

name: Form Usability
description: Forms are easy to complete because fields, labels, validation, formatting, required inputs, and submission behavior are clear.
aliases: forms| input fields| validation| data entry
examples: The form clearly marked required fields.  I did not know the expected phone number format.  The inline validation helped me correct mistakes.

name: Input Flexibility
description: The system accepts reasonable variations in user input, supports correction, and does not force unnecessarily rigid formats.
aliases: flexible input| tolerant input| format forgiveness| correction
examples: The date field accepted both typed and selected dates.  The search worked despite a typo.  I had to reformat the value manually.

name: Consistency and Standards
description: The interface behaves consistently across pages and follows familiar web conventions, reducing the need to relearn interactions.
aliases: consistency| conventions| standards| predictability
examples: The same icon worked the same way everywhere.  The checkout flow matched what I expected.  Similar buttons behaved differently on different pages.

name: Memorability
description: Returning users can remember how to use the interface after time away because patterns, labels, and workflows are stable and recognizable.
aliases: rememberability| return use| recall| familiarity
examples: I came back after a week and still knew where to go.  I forgot how to access the report.  The layout was familiar from my last visit.

name: Recognition Over Recall
description: The interface reduces memory burden by showing options, context, history, suggestions, and visible cues instead of requiring users to remember details.
aliases: memory support| visible options| cues| recognition
examples: Recent searches helped me find the item again.  I had to remember the exact command name.  Suggested values made the form easier to complete.

name: Accessibility
description: The website or web application can be used by people with diverse abilities, assistive technologies, devices, and interaction needs.
aliases: a11y| inclusive design| assistive technology| universal access
examples: The page worked well with keyboard navigation.  The contrast made the text hard to read.  The image buttons were missing accessible labels.

name: Keyboard Accessibility
description: Users can navigate and operate the interface using only a keyboard, with logical focus order and visible focus indicators.
aliases: keyboard support| focus management| tab navigation| non-mouse access
examples: I could tab through the form in order.  The focus indicator was visible.  I got trapped inside the modal.

name: Screen Reader Support
description: The interface provides meaningful structure, labels, roles, and announcements for users relying on screen readers.
aliases: screen readers| ARIA| semantic markup| assistive labels
examples: The screen reader announced the error message.  The button was read as unlabeled.  Headings made the page easy to navigate.

name: Color and Contrast
description: Text, controls, icons, and states have sufficient contrast and do not rely on color alone to communicate meaning.
aliases: contrast| color accessibility| visual legibility| color reliance
examples: The error was shown with both text and color.  The gray text was difficult to read.  I could not tell the selected option by color alone.

name: Responsive Design
description: The interface adapts effectively across screen sizes, orientations, browsers, and devices without losing usability.
aliases: mobile usability| adaptive layout| cross-device| responsive layout
examples: The page worked well on my phone.  The table overflowed on mobile.  The menu was easier to use on desktop than tablet.

name: Performance and Responsiveness
description: Pages, interactions, searches, uploads, and transitions feel fast enough to support user flow without frustration or uncertainty.
aliases: speed| loading time| responsiveness| latency
examples: The dashboard loaded quickly.  The page froze after I clicked save.  The search results took too long to appear.

name: Reliability and Stability
description: The system behaves dependably without crashes, broken links, missing content, unexpected resets, or inconsistent availability.
aliases: stability| dependability| bugs| broken behavior
examples: The page crashed when I uploaded a file.  Links opened the expected pages.  My changes were saved correctly.

name: User Control and Freedom
description: Users can undo, cancel, go back, edit, exit, or change decisions without being trapped or punished by the interface.
aliases: control| undo| cancel| reversibility| freedom
examples: I could cancel the process without losing everything.  There was no way to undo the deletion.  I could edit my answer before submitting.

name: Personalization and Preferences
description: The system lets users adjust relevant settings, views, notifications, language, display, or workflows to fit their needs.
aliases: customization| preferences| settings| user choice
examples: I changed the notification settings easily.  The dashboard let me choose what to see first.  I could not turn off irrelevant alerts.

name: Trust and Transparency
description: The interface makes system behavior, data usage, pricing, permissions, automation, and consequences clear enough for users to feel confident.
aliases: transparency| trust| explainability| disclosure
examples: The app explained why it needed permission.  I understood what would happen after clicking publish.  The pricing information felt hidden.

name: Privacy and Security Usability
description: Security and privacy controls are understandable, discoverable, and usable without creating unnecessary friction or confusion.
aliases: privacy controls| security settings| permissions| account safety
examples: I found the privacy settings quickly.  The permission request was clear.  I was unsure who could see my profile.

name: Help and Documentation
description: Users can access relevant help, examples, FAQs, support, or contextual assistance when they need it.
aliases: help| support| documentation| guidance
examples: The help article matched my problem.  The FAQ was easy to search.  I could not find support from the error page.

name: Satisfaction
description: The experience feels pleasant, polished, useful, and aligned with user expectations, creating positive emotional response and confidence.
aliases: delight| perceived quality| comfort| user satisfaction
examples: The interface felt clean and professional.  I enjoyed using the dashboard.  The experience felt clunky and frustrating.

name: Emotional Friction
description: The interface causes frustration, anxiety, doubt, annoyance, impatience, or loss of confidence during use.
aliases: frustration| anxiety| annoyance| emotional response
examples: I felt nervous before submitting because the consequences were unclear.  The repeated errors were frustrating.  The process made me feel confident.

name: Visual Design Quality
description: The interface looks coherent, polished, and appropriate for its purpose, supporting comprehension and perceived credibility.
aliases: visual polish| aesthetics| UI quality| presentation
examples: The design looked modern and trustworthy.  The inconsistent spacing made the page feel unfinished.  The icons made the interface easier to scan.

name: Data Presentation
description: Tables, charts, summaries, cards, and visualizations communicate information clearly and support interpretation, comparison, and decision-making.
aliases: data clarity| reporting| visualization| summaries
examples: The chart made the trend obvious.  The table had too many columns to scan.  The summary helped me understand the results quickly.

name: Empty States
description: Screens with no data, no results, or unfinished setup explain the situation and guide users toward a useful next action.
aliases: no results| empty screen| blank state| zero state
examples: The empty dashboard told me how to create my first project.  Search returned no results but suggested alternatives.  The page was blank and I did not know why.

name: Notifications and Alerts
description: Messages, reminders, warnings, and alerts are timely, relevant, understandable, and not overwhelming.
aliases: alerts| reminders| messages| interruptions
examples: The warning appeared before the risky action.  I received too many irrelevant notifications.  The alert clearly explained what changed.

name: Internationalization and Localization
description: The interface supports users across languages, regions, formats, cultural expectations, and local conventions.
aliases: localization| language| regional formats| i18n
examples: The date format matched my region.  Some translated labels sounded unnatural.  The currency was shown clearly.

name: Account and Authentication Usability
description: Signing up, logging in, recovering access, managing sessions, and handling authentication are clear and low-friction while remaining secure.
aliases: login| signup| authentication| account access
examples: Password recovery was straightforward.  I was logged out without warning.  The signup form asked for too much too soon.

name: Permission and Role Clarity
description: Users understand what they can access, what actions they are allowed to take, and why some features are restricted.
aliases: roles| permissions| access control| authorization
examples: The app explained why I could not edit the study.  I knew which actions were available to admins.  A disabled button appeared with no explanation.

name: Mobile Interaction Usability
description: Touch targets, gestures, scrolling, forms, menus, and mobile-specific interactions are comfortable and predictable on phones and tablets.
aliases: touch usability| mobile interaction| gestures| tap targets
examples: The buttons were large enough to tap.  The menu was hard to open on mobile.  The swipe gesture was not obvious.

name: Content Relevance
description: The interface shows information, options, and recommendations that are relevant to the user’s current goal, role, or context.
aliases: relevance| contextual content| useful information| prioritization
examples: The dashboard showed the studies I needed first.  I saw options that did not apply to my role.  The recommendations matched what I was trying to do.

name: Decision Support
description: The interface helps users compare options, understand tradeoffs, and make confident decisions without excessive cognitive effort.
aliases: choice support| comparison| decision clarity| guidance
examples: The comparison table helped me choose a plan.  I did not understand which option was best for me.  The summary made the decision easier.

name: Cognitive Load
description: The interface avoids overwhelming users with too many choices, dense information, unclear steps, or unnecessary mental effort.
aliases: mental effort| complexity| overload| cognitive burden
examples: There were too many options on one screen.  The step-by-step flow reduced confusion.  I had to think too hard to understand the page.

name: Progressive Disclosure
description: The interface reveals advanced or secondary information only when needed, keeping primary workflows simple while preserving access to detail.
aliases: advanced options| disclosure| details on demand| simplification
examples: The advanced settings were hidden until I needed them.  The page showed too many technical options upfront.  Expanding the section revealed useful details.

name: Affordance and Discoverability
description: Interactive elements look interactive, available actions are easy to discover, and users can tell how to operate controls.
aliases: discoverability| affordance| interactive cues| action visibility
examples: The card looked clickable.  I did not realize the icon opened a menu.  The drag handle made the interaction obvious.

name: State Visibility
description: The interface clearly shows selected, active, disabled, expanded, collapsed, saved, unsaved, completed, or pending states.
aliases: state clarity| selected state| active state| status indication
examples: The selected filter was obvious.  I could not tell whether the toggle was on or off.  The draft showed an unsaved changes warning.

name: Recoverability from Navigation
description: Users can move between pages, return to previous states, and recover from accidental navigation without losing work or context.
aliases: back behavior| navigation recovery| context preservation| history
examples: The back button returned me to the same filtered list.  I lost my form after opening another page.  The app remembered where I was.

name: Accessibility of Dynamic Content
description: Changes caused by modals, live updates, validation, filters, or asynchronous loading are communicated accessibly and do not disorient users.
aliases: dynamic updates| live regions| modal accessibility| async feedback
examples: The modal focused on the first actionable control.  New results appeared without explanation.  The screen reader announced that the upload was complete.

name: Findability of Key Actions
description: Important actions are located where users expect them and are visually prominent enough to support task completion.
aliases: action discoverability| primary actions| CTA visibility| action placement
examples: The save button was exactly where I expected.  I had trouble finding how to export the report.  The main action was hidden under a secondary menu.

name: Instructional Clarity
description: Task instructions, requirements, constraints, and next steps are stated clearly before users act.
aliases: instructions| requirements| task guidance| clarity
examples: The upload requirements were explained before I selected a file.  I did not know what information the field required.  The next step was clearly stated.

name: Undo and Confirmation
description: The interface provides appropriate confirmations for destructive actions and undo options for reversible actions.
aliases: undo| confirmation| destructive action| safety net
examples: The undo snackbar let me restore the deleted item.  The app asked me to confirm before deleting.  I deleted the record with one accidental click.

name: User Confidence
description: The experience gives users confidence that they are doing the right thing, that their data is safe, and that outcomes match expectations.
aliases: confidence| reassurance| certainty| perceived control
examples: The preview made me confident before publishing.  I was unsure whether my changes were saved.  The confirmation message reassured me.
